### `politico_eco_bbs_reports`

Stores every abuse report action for content (posts or comments) or user,
recording reporting user, target, type/reason, status, actor chain, and
associated timestamps. Central to the moderation event lifecycle,
enabling time-based review, escalation, and outcome tracking. Related to
[politico_eco_bbs_report_status_logs](#politico_eco_bbs_report_status_logs) for status/audit, {@link
politico_eco_bbs_blinds} for enforcement, and references user/content
tables via FKs for context integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `reporting_user_id`
  > Reporting user's [politico_eco_bbs_users.id](#politico_eco_bbs_users). Who submitted the
  > report.
- `target_post_id`
  > Target post's [politico_eco_bbs_posts.id](#politico_eco_bbs_posts) if report is about a
  > post. Nullable for non-post reports.
- `target_comment_id`
  > Target comment's [politico_eco_bbs_comments.id](#politico_eco_bbs_comments) if report is about
  > a comment. Nullable for non-comment reports.
- `target_user_id`
  > Target user's [politico_eco_bbs_users.id](#politico_eco_bbs_users) if the report concerns a
  > user (i.e., harassment, impersonation). Nullable where not applicable.
- `reported_reason`
  > The reason/type selected by reporting user (e.g. spam, abuse,
  > misinformation, etc).
- `detail`
  > Freeform description or evidence by reporter. May contain URLs, specific
  > context.
- `status`
  > Current status of the report (open, reviewed, blind_applied,
  > warning_issued, escalation, closed, etc). Used to determine moderation
  > workflow state.
- `created_at`: UTC datetime when report was submitted.
- `updated_at`
  > UTC datetime when the report entity was last updated by
  > system/process/action.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp, if the report was voided or retracted. Null
  > otherwise.

### `politico_eco_bbs_report_status_logs`

Tracks every status or significant field change for a given abuse report,
maintaining an audit trail for all moderation actions (assign, review,
blind, warn, escalate, close, etc). Enables precise procedural
accountability, rollback investigation, and process improvement
analytics. Each log record references a specific report via FK and
optionally records the moderator/admin actor responsible.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `report_id`
  > Target report's [politico_eco_bbs_reports.id](#politico_eco_bbs_reports). The abuse report
  > under status update/audit.
- `actor_moderator_id`
  > Moderator's [politico_eco_bbs_moderators.id](#politico_eco_bbs_moderators) if a moderator
  > performed the action. Nullable if action taken by automation/admin.
- `actor_admin_id`
  > Admin's [politico_eco_bbs_admins.id](#politico_eco_bbs_admins) if an admin performed the
  > action. Nullable if not applicable.
- `from_status`: Status value before the action (e.g. open, reviewed, blind_applied, etc).
- `to_status`
  > Status value after the action. Captures the moderation workflow
  > transition.
- `action_verb`
  > The action taken (assign, review, blind, warn, escalate, close, etc) as
  > granularity for audit.
- `action_detail`
  > Detailed explanation, notes, or reason for the action. Often used for
  > audit justification.
- `created_at`: UTC datetime when this log/event was recorded.

### `politico_eco_bbs_blinds`

Represents application of blind (hide) status on reported or
policy-violating content. Connects to reports, target content/user, and
issuing moderator/admin. Records scope, rationale, and enforced timespan.
Critical for transparency and restoring trust in policy enforcement
decisions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `report_id`
  > Reference to generating abuse report's {@link
  > politico_eco_bbs_reports.id} that justified the blind action. Nullable
  > for policy/manual blinds.
- `target_post_id`
  > Blind applied post's [politico_eco_bbs_posts.id](#politico_eco_bbs_posts). Nullable for
  > user/comment-wide blinds.
- `target_comment_id`
  > Blind applied comment's [politico_eco_bbs_comments.id](#politico_eco_bbs_comments). Nullable
  > for post/user-wide blinds.
- `target_user_id`
  > Blind applied user's [politico_eco_bbs_users.id](#politico_eco_bbs_users) (user
  > restriction). Nullable for content-only blinds.
- `actor_moderator_id`: Issuing moderator's [politico_eco_bbs_moderators.id](#politico_eco_bbs_moderators).
- `actor_admin_id`
  > Issuing admin's [politico_eco_bbs_admins.id](#politico_eco_bbs_admins). Nullable if not
  > issued by admin.
- `scope`
  > Scope of blind (e.g. post, comment, user, all_content). Indicates what
  > was hidden by policy enforcement.
- `reason`: Explanation or policy type for why the blind was enforced.
- `start_time`: Timestamp when blind took effect.
- `end_time`: Timestamp when blind was lifted/expired. Nullable if still in effect.
- `created_at`: When the blind record was written.
- `updated_at`: When the blind record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp, if the blind was reversed/deleted. Null
  > otherwise.

### `politico_eco_bbs_warnings`

Tracks all punitive warnings delivered to users following moderation
review/escalation chained to reports. Records which report, what
content/user is being warned/who issued warning, and explanatory
message/justification. Crucial for progressive moderation history and
enforcing repeated offense policy.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `report_id`
  > Origin report's [politico_eco_bbs_reports.id](#politico_eco_bbs_reports) spawning the warning.
  > May be null for manual warnings.
- `target_user_id`: Target warned user's [politico_eco_bbs_users.id](#politico_eco_bbs_users).
- `actor_moderator_id`: Issuing moderator's [politico_eco_bbs_moderators.id](#politico_eco_bbs_moderators).
- `actor_admin_id`
  > Issuing admin's [politico_eco_bbs_admins.id](#politico_eco_bbs_admins). Nullable if not
  > issued by admin.
- `warn_reason`: Explanation provided to user on why this warning applies.
- `context`: Further details on what specific behavior or content was in violation.
- `created_at`: Issue timestamp of the warning.

### `politico_eco_bbs_escalations`

Stores escalation events—when moderation or admin review and intervention
are required above standard report workflow (e.g. for urgent
policy/abuse/legal cases). Connects to the original report, target,
escalation initiator and reviewer/decider, rationale/timeline, and
outcome notes. Central for compliance and governance reporting.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `report_id`
  > Underlying report's [politico_eco_bbs_reports.id](#politico_eco_bbs_reports) at source of
  > escalation.
- `initiator_user_id`
  > Escalation initiator's [politico_eco_bbs_users.id](#politico_eco_bbs_users) (mod or admin
  > who flagged escalation).
- `reviewer_admin_id`
  > Reviewer or ultimate authority admin's [politico_eco_bbs_admins.id](#politico_eco_bbs_admins)
  > for final escalation disposition.
- `escalation_reason`
  > Why escalation was required (e.g. urgent risk, legal, repeated abuse,
  > pattern match).
- `rationale_detail`: Supporting detail for compliance or legal trace.
- `outcome_status`: Final outcome of escalation (approved, denied, further_action, etc).
- `created_at`: Timezone-aware timestamp when escalation was created.
- `updated_at`: When the escalation record was last updated.

### `politico_eco_bbs_auth_logs`

Authentication event logs for politico-eco-bbs. Captures successful and
failed login, logout, token, and session actions for all member roles
(user, moderator, admin). Used for security audit trails, fraud
investigation, incident response, and compliance review. May reference
the user, moderator, or admin who triggered the event and related
metadata including IP, user agent, result code, grant/deny reason, and
session context.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`
  > Reference to the acting user's [politico_eco_bbs_users.id](#politico_eco_bbs_users), if role
  > is user.
- `moderator_id`
  > Reference to the acting moderator's {@link
  > politico_eco_bbs_moderators.id}, if role is moderator.
- `admin_id`
  > Reference to the acting admin's [politico_eco_bbs_admins.id](#politico_eco_bbs_admins), if
  > role is admin.
- `event_type`
  > Type of authentication event (e.g., login, logout, token_issued,
  > token_revoked, password_reset_attempt, etc.).
- `identifier`
  > User identifier used for authentication (e.g., username, email, external
  > id).
- `ip_address`: IP address from which the authentication event was initiated.
- `user_agent`: HTTP user agent string at the time of event.
- `result_code`
  > System/HTTP result code after event attempt (e.g., success, fail, locked,
  > throttled, etc.).
- `result_message`: Summary or detail of auth result; error message if failed.
- `session_id`
  > Session or token id associated with the authentication event, if
  > applicable.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the authentication event occurred.

### `politico_eco_bbs_access_logs`

Access logs covering resource access or actions by all users, moderators,
and admins within politico-eco-bbs. Captures full audit trail for every
critical page/API/feature access. Used for forensic analysis, monitoring,
abuse/incident review, security audits, and policy compliance
traceability. References actor details and targeted resource.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`
  > Reference to the acting user's [politico_eco_bbs_users.id](#politico_eco_bbs_users), if role
  > is user.
- `moderator_id`
  > Reference to the acting moderator's {@link
  > politico_eco_bbs_moderators.id}, if role is moderator.
- `admin_id`
  > Reference to the acting admin's [politico_eco_bbs_admins.id](#politico_eco_bbs_admins), if
  > role is admin.
- `resource_type`
  > Type of resource accessed (e.g., post, comment, policy_page, settings,
  > admin_panel, API, etc.).
- `resource_id`
  > Primary key, UUID, or composite string ID of resource accessed; can be
  > null for general access logs.
- `action`
  > Business-aware action performed on the resource (e.g., view, edit,
  > update, delete, blind, warn, escalate, export, etc.).
- `target_ip`: Originating IP address involved in the access or action.
- `user_agent`: HTTP user agent of the actor for this access event.
- `outcome_code`
  > Access result or HTTP/system outcome (success, forbidden, error,
  > throttled, blocked, etc.).
- `outcome_message`: Detail of access result or error, if applicable.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when access or resource action occurred.

### `politico_eco_bbs_policy_change_logs`

Logs for policy, configuration, and permission changes within
politico-eco-bbs. Captures all admin or moderator events that affect
roles, policy documents, system/board configuration, permissions,
category/rule/setting changes, filter definitions, or escalation
triggers. Used for compliance trace, rollback planning, audit and
responsibility assignment for any security or regulatory decision.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`
  > Reference to admin responsible for the policy change. {@link
  > politico_eco_bbs_admins.id}.
- `moderator_id`
  > Reference to moderator triggering the policy change (rare). {@link
  > politico_eco_bbs_moderators.id}.
- `change_type`
  > Type/category of the policy or config change (e.g., permission_update,
  > escalation_rule, legal_policy, system_setting, category_edit, etc.).
- `object_type`
  > What entity/type was affected (setting, category, filter, permission,
  > etc.).
- `object_id`
  > Object/setting/category/rule ID affected; may be null for top-level
  > policy changes.
- `before_value`
  > Value/info before the change (JSON/BLOB if complex); used for
  > rollback/audit comparison.
- `after_value`
  > Value/info after the change (JSON/BLOB if complex); used for audit and
  > diff review.
- `change_reason`: Human or system-provided reason/rationale for the change.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of the policy/config change event.

### `politico_eco_bbs_error_logs`

Logs of detected or non-recovered application errors within
politico-eco-bbs, such as backend exception, failed workflow, audit
alert, lost resource, or blocked operation. Used for root cause analysis,
error resolution, debugging, incident response, and audit compliance.
Provides developer- and admin-ready event context, containing stack
trace, attached object/ref, actor, and traceable metadata.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`
  > Reference to user who encountered the error (if known). {@link

  > Reference to admin associated with the error event (if present). {@link
  > politico_eco_bbs_admins.id}.

  > [politico_eco_bbs_moderators.id](#politico_eco_bbs_moderators).
- `error_type`
  > Classifier for error event (e.g., backend_exception, validation_failed,
  > timeout, not_found, permission_denied, etc.).
- `severity`: Severity code (e.g., info, warning, error, fatal).
- `reference_id`
  > ID of the subject/resource most closely associated with the error event,
  > if any.
- `method`: Method or API endpoint where the error occurred.
- `user_agent`: User agent involved, if relevant.
- `stack_trace`: Error/exception stack trace, if captured.
- `message`: Error message or summary suitable for user/ops/diagnostics/audit.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when the error was recorded.

### `politico_eco_bbs_kpi_snapshots`

Regular periodic snapshots of platform-wide KPIs for politico-eco-bbs,
such as DAU, MAU, growth, engagement, report rates, and retention
statistics. This table aggregates critical business metrics at fixed
intervals for reporting, analysis, and anomaly detection. Used for
historical KPI trend analysis, quarterly/annual reviews, and dashboard
reporting. No direct FK to users or content; covers macro-level,
system-wide statistics only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `kpi_period_start`: Start of the KPI aggregation period (typically midnight).
- `kpi_period_end`: End of the KPI aggregation period (exclusive bound).
- `dau_count`: Daily Active Users for the period.
- `mau_count`: Monthly Active Users for the period.
- `new_user_count`: Number of new user signups in the period.
- `retention_1d_rate`: 1-day retention rate for the period (as a fraction, not percent).
- `retention_7d_rate`: 7-day retention rate for the period (as a fraction).
- `retention_30d_rate`: 30-day retention rate for the period (as a fraction).
- `avg_post_per_user`: Average number of posts per user during the aggregation period.
- `avg_comment_per_user`: Average number of comments per user during the aggregation period.
- `report_count`: Total report events counted in the period.
- `blind_count`: Total moderation blinds (content hidden or moderated) in the period.
- `churn_user_count`: Number of users considered churned (no longer active) in the period.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of snapshot creation.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update (aggregation/correction).

### `politico_eco_bbs_user_activity_metrics`

Aggregated periodic user activity metrics for reporting, analytics, and
behavioral analysis. Tracks key activity data for each user, such as
number of posts, comments, logins, likes, dislikes, average session time,
first activity, and more during a given period. Used to identify
active/inactive users, engagement level, power users, and retention
analysis. References the base user table for relationships but not user
PII.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`: Target user's [politico_eco_bbs_users.id](#politico_eco_bbs_users).
- `metric_period_start`: Start of the activity aggregation period.
- `metric_period_end`: End of the aggregation period (exclusive bound).
- `post_count`: Number of posts created by the user during the period.
- `comment_count`: Number of comments made by the user during the period.
- `login_count`: Number of successful logins by the user during the aggregation period.
- `like_count`: Number of likes submitted by the user during the aggregation period.
- `dislike_count`: Number of dislikes submitted by the user during the aggregation period.
- `avg_session_seconds`
  > Average session time in seconds the user spent on the platform in the
  > period.
- `first_activity_at`: Datetime of the user's first measurable activity in this period.
- `last_activity_at`: Datetime of the user's last activity in this period.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of metric row creation.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update to metric row.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (row is inactive if non-null).

### `politico_eco_bbs_content_traffic_metrics`

Aggregates and snapshots content (post/comment/category) level traffic
metrics (views, likes, dislikes, engagement, etc) for a reporting window.
Used for traffic analytics, content performance dashboards, reporting of
most/least engaged content, and trend monitoring. Allows
multi-dimensional queries by time, content type, and category. FKs to
posts, comments, and categories as appropriate; null when not applicable
(e.g., view/interaction at category level).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`
  > Target post's [politico_eco_bbs_posts.id](#politico_eco_bbs_posts), if this metric is for a
  > post. Nullable when metric is for comment or category.
- `comment_id`
  > Target comment's [politico_eco_bbs_comments.id](#politico_eco_bbs_comments), if this metric
  > relates to a comment. Nullable otherwise.
- `category_id`
  > Target category's [politico_eco_bbs_categories.id](#politico_eco_bbs_categories), if content
  > metric is at category level. Nullable if not relevant.
- `metric_period_start`: Start of aggregation period for these metrics.
- `metric_period_end`: End of aggregation period (exclusive bound).
- `view_count`: Total number of views for the content during the period.
- `unique_visitor_count`: Count of unique visitors viewing the content in the period.
- `like_count`: Total likes the content received during the period.
- `dislike_count`: Total dislikes received for the period.
- `comment_count`
  > Total comments received by this content within the period (posts or
  > categories).
- `report_count`: Number of reports submitted against this content in period.
- `blind_count`: Number of times the content was blinded (moderated) during the period.
- `engagement_rate`: Engagement rate (interactions per view) for the period.
- `bounce_rate`: Rate of single-view exits (user did not engage) for the period.
- `created_at`: Metric creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Metric last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (marks row as inactive if set).

### `politico_eco_bbs_retention_metrics`

Cohort and retention analytics snapshots for politico-eco-bbs. Stores
aggregates and rates by cohort (e.g. signup week/month), period, and
metric dimension. Enables analysis of user retention, cohort growth,
churn, and long-term engagement. Rows are immutable snapshots for
interval reporting and historical trend analysis.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `retention_period_start`
  > Start date/time of the analytic retention window (e.g., a day, week, or
  > month).
- `retention_period_end`: End date/time of the retention window (exclusive bound).
- `cohort_type`
  > Name/type of the cohort grouping (e.g., 'signup_week', 'signup_month',
  > 'campaign').
- `cohort_id`
  > Value identifier for the cohort (e.g., week number '2024-W31', month
  > '2024-08', or campaign name).
- `cohort_size`: Total users in the cohort at the start of the window.
- `retained_count_1d`: Number of cohort users retained at 1-day mark in period.
- `retained_count_7d`: Number of cohort users retained at 7-day mark.
- `retained_count_30d`: Number of cohort users retained at 30-day mark.
- `churn_count`: Number of users lost/churned from the cohort in the period.
- `retention_rate_1d`: 1-day retention rate for this cohort snapshot.
- `retention_rate_7d`: 7-day retention rate for this cohort.
- `retention_rate_30d`: 30-day retention rate for this cohort.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for retention metric snapshot creation.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for this metric row.

### `politico_eco_bbs_risk_events`

Root table storing each recorded risk/compliance incident (e.g., policy
violation, data breach attempt, regulatory event, security issue, or any
incident requiring formal compliance review). Each entry represents a
unique occurrence under the scope of legal/audit review. Linked by
foreign keys to user/admin tables for originators, responsible parties,
and context actors (from already-existing user tables). Serves as the
audit root for other compliance models (audits, evidence, escalations).
Fully normalized, retaining historical/amendment fields and traceable
change chain for regulatory inspection.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `creator_user_id`: Originator of the risk event. [politico_eco_bbs_users.id](#politico_eco_bbs_users)
- `assigned_admin_id`
  > Admin or compliance officer assigned to review or resolve the event.
  > [politico_eco_bbs_admins.id](#politico_eco_bbs_admins)
- `type`
  > Event type (e.g., 'policy_violation', 'system_abuse',
  > 'security_incident', 'legal_notice'). Enumerated at application layer.
  > Enables categorization for compliance reporting.
- `status`
  > Lifecycle status of the risk event (e.g., 'open', 'under_review',
  > 'resolved', 'closed', 'escalated'). String (enum-limited at app layer),
  > used for workflow control and audit.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of the risk/incident, context, or observed
  > abnormality—used for compliance investigation and regulatory reviews.
- `regulatory_reference`
  > Relevant law, standard, compliance reference, or policy article ID (e.g.,
  > 'PIPA-28', 'GDPR-33', 'service_policy-3.2', etc). Enables downstream
  > mapping to compliance frameworks. Nullable if non-regulatory.
- `detected_at`
  > Original datetime the risk event or abnormality was detected. For audit
  > chains and incident forensics.
- `resolved_at`
  > Timestamp when the event was marked resolved by compliance/admin action.
  > Stays null until fully actioned and closed.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp (immutable).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (set on each change).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft-delete timestamp (null if active, set if archived/deleted for
  > retention/audit only).

### `politico_eco_bbs_compliance_audits`

Formal compliance audit or internal/external review record tied to a
specific risk event, supporting governance and regulatory traceability.
Each record represents a completed audit step, stating findings,
reviewer, result, and any prescriptive advice. Enables fine-grained
tracking of all assessments, requirements, or external audits for risk
events (including regulatory, security, and legal reviews). Credentials
all actions for future evidence, precedent, or recurring issue analysis.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `risk_event_id`: The risk event under review. [politico_eco_bbs_risk_events.id](#politico_eco_bbs_risk_events)
- `reviewer_admin_id`
  > Admin or compliance officer conducting the audit. {@link
  > politico_eco_bbs_admins.id}
- `audit_type`
  > Type of audit or review conducted (e.g., 'regulatory', 'security',
  > 'internal', 'external', 'recurring_review'). Used for compliance mapping
  > and reporting.
- `findings`
  > Findings or outcome of the audit/review (text summary of issues,
  > compliance gaps, or passes). Used for compliance management, improvement,
  > and reporting.
- `recommendations`
  > Recommended actions or next steps based on audit outcome (prescriptive,
  > can be empty string if no advice).
- `regulation_reference`
  > Regulatory article, law, or compliance framework referenced by the audit
  > (GDPR, PIPA, ISO27001, etc). Optional if review was not governed by a
  > standard.
- `audited_at`
  > Date and time at which the audit/review was formally completed. Used for
  > traceability and evidence chain.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp (immutable).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (set on each change).
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp. Null if active; set for audit chain retention.

### `politico_eco_bbs_evidence_files`

Evidence or supporting files (immutable attachments) for risk events
and/or compliance audits. Allows traceable chain-of-custody of
screenshots, logs, scanned documents, or forensic files required for
legal/compliance proofs. Each record is immutable, stores source file
metadata and structural link to either a risk event or a compliance
audit. File storage URI is strictly separated from attachment flows for
routine user-content. Important for regulatory examination, litigation,
or dispute forensics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `risk_event_id`
  > Linked risk event if evidence is attached to a risk/compliance incident.
  > [politico_eco_bbs_risk_events.id](#politico_eco_bbs_risk_events)
- `compliance_audit_id`
  > Linked audit if evidence is tied directly to an audit step (not
  > mandatory). [politico_eco_bbs_compliance_audits.id](#politico_eco_bbs_compliance_audits)
- `uploader_admin_id`
  > Admin uploading/providing the evidence file to the compliance chain.
  > [politico_eco_bbs_admins.id](#politico_eco_bbs_admins)
- `file_uri`
  > Secure URI of evidence or proof file. Not reused with user content
  > attachment system; for compliance-only files.
- `mime_type`
  > MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'image/png').
  > Compliance chain requires this for examination and chain-of-custody
  > validations.
- `file_size_bytes`
  > File size in bytes (integer, for audit/evidence storage management, cap
  > enforcement).
- `file_description`
  > Free-text description of evidence contents/purpose (e.g., 'network log
  > before incident', 'email screenshot', 'regulatory notice scan', etc).
  > Used in compliance reviews.
- `uploaded_at`
  > Timestamp when the file was uploaded or registered to the record
  > (immutable). For compliance/audit control.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft-deletion timestamp (null if active; set for chain-of-custody audits
  > and retention compliance).

### `politico_eco_bbs_legal_escalations`

Formal table recording all legal or regulatory escalations arising from
risk events (e.g., court, police, regulator, or external compliance
authority involvement). Tracks the escalation chain, status, responsible
admin, referenced compliance or legal codes, involved parties, and
resolution outcomes. Used for long-term compliance proof, legal defense,
and regulatory audit. Each record strictly references a risk event and
(optionally) a compliance audit, and documents lifecycle for full
chain-of-custody, evidence, and external notification requirements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `risk_event_id`
  > Risk event which triggered the escalation process. {@link
  > politico_eco_bbs_risk_events.id}
- `audit_reference_id`
  > Optional reference to the compliance audit directly leading to this
  > escalation. [politico_eco_bbs_compliance_audits.id](#politico_eco_bbs_compliance_audits)
- `initiator_admin_id`
  > Admin responsible for formal escalation (typically DPO or senior
  > compliance/legal). [politico_eco_bbs_admins.id](#politico_eco_bbs_admins)
- `escalation_type`
  > Class of legal escalation (e.g., 'court_filing', 'police_report',
  > 'regulator_notification', 'third_party_complaint', etc). Allows reporting
  > and policy mapping.
- `external_authority`
  > Short name/title of the external authority or body notified in the
  > escalation (e.g., 'Seoul Eastern District Court', 'KISA', 'NPA', etc).
  > Used for regulatory chain.
- `case_reference`
  > Official case or docket number assigned by the external authority/court.
  > Optional if not yet issued.
- `status`
  > Status of the escalation process (e.g., 'pending', 'in_review',
  > 'resolved', 'dismissed', 'no_action', etc). String for workflow tracking
  > and compliance documentation.
- `outcome`
  > Describes the final, intermediate, or current result of the escalation
  > (e.g., 'regulator warning issued', 'case dismissed', 'court ruling: in
  > favor', 'pending reply', etc). Essential for full compliance evidence.
- `initiated_at`
  > When the escalation process was originally initiated/submitted. Used for
  > legal/audit time-chaining.
- `finalized_at`
  > Date/time escalation was definitively closed, receives outcome,
  > dismissed, or otherwise finalized (null if ongoing). For
  > chain-of-custody, legal proof.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp (immutable).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (set on each change).
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp. Null if active; set for legal chain retention.
